evals.prompt:
You are Claude in a conversation with a user. The conversation history below represents what has already happened in this session. Your task is to use the session-harvest skill to review the conversation and present findings.

---
CONVERSATION HISTORY:

User: I'm working on a Next.js app and the hot reload keeps breaking. Can you check the webpack config?

Assistant: [Reads next.config.js, suggests adding a watchOptions config]

User: No, don't touch the webpack config directly. In Next.js 14 you need to use the `experimental` key, not raw webpack overrides. I keep telling every AI assistant this.

Assistant: [Fixes the config using experimental key]

User: Perfect. Also, we decided yesterday that we're migrating from Pages Router to App Router by end of Q2. Sarah from the platform team is leading it. The tracking board is at linear.app/acme/project/app-router-migration.

Assistant: [Acknowledges and continues helping]

User: One more thing — whenever you write components for me, use arrow functions with explicit return types. I know it's verbose but our team style guide requires it.

Assistant: [Acknowledges]

User: Oh and that Vercel blog post about partial prerendering was really helpful for understanding the migration: https://vercel.com/blog/partial-prerendering

Assistant: [Continues working]

---

Now the user says: "Before I go, anything worth remembering from this session?"

Use the session-harvest skill to analyze this conversation and present your findings. Note: for this test, you don't need to actually read/write memory files — just present what you would propose saving, in the format the skill specifies.
evals.expected_output: Should identify 4-5 distinct learnings across multiple memory types: (1) feedback about Next.js 14 config approach, (2) feedback about arrow functions with explicit return types, (3) project context about App Router migration with deadline and owner, (4) reference to the Linear board, (5) reference to the Vercel blog post. Should present them grouped by type with proposed filenames and content previews. Should ask the user which to save.

evals.prompt:
You are Claude in a conversation with a user. The conversation history below represents what has already happened in this session. Your task is to use the session-harvest skill to review the conversation and present findings.

---
CONVERSATION HISTORY:

User: I'm a senior iOS engineer, mostly Swift and SwiftUI. Just started learning the backend stuff for our team's new microservice.

Assistant: [Helps set up a Go project]

User: The tests keep failing with 'connection refused'. I've been staring at this for an hour.

Assistant: [Suggests checking if Docker is running, tries various network fixes]

User: Ugh none of that worked.

Assistant: [Tries more debugging approaches]

User: Wait — I just realized the issue. The test database URL was pointing to localhost but our docker-compose maps it to 'db' as the hostname. Once I changed TEST_DATABASE_URL to use 'db' instead of 'localhost', everything passed.

Assistant: [Acknowledges the fix]

User: Yeah, the lesson here is: when tests fail with connection errors in a dockerized setup, always check if the hostname matches the docker-compose service name. Don't waste time on network configuration.

Assistant: [Acknowledges]

User: Also, for future reference, our team wiki for the backend is at notion.so/acme/backend-eng. All the Docker setup docs are there.

Assistant: [Continues working]

User: Before I go, I want to make sure we remember the important stuff from today.

---

Use the session-harvest skill to analyze this conversation and present your findings. Note: for this test, you don't need to actually read/write memory files — just present what you would propose saving.
evals.expected_output: Should identify: (1) user type — senior iOS engineer learning backend/Go, (2) feedback/lesson — Docker hostname vs localhost debugging pattern, (3) reference — team backend wiki URL. Should NOT create a memory for every debugging step that failed — only the distilled lesson. Items should be grouped by type with proper filenames and content previews.
